clue.text: Need one remind him to "drop the catch"?

definitions.text: Need one remind him to "drop the catch

parts.words: Need one remind him to "drop the catch
parts.note: a reminder to drop a catch is pointless for a clumsy fielder, who drops catches without being told

explanation.surface: A sarcastic question about a fielder who is forever spilling catches.
explanation.definitionFit: A clumsy person who keeps dropping things is called this, especially a cricketer who drops catches.

clue.text: Quiet ghost has been disturbed? Fallacious way to argue

indicators.note: the letters of the three words are stirred up and set in a new order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A peaceful spirit has been stirred up from its rest.
explanation.walkthrough: 'disturbed' rearranges QUIET, GHOST and BEEN; 'has' only links them.
explanation.definitionFit: Assuming the very point to be proved is the classic logical fallacy of circular reasoning.

clue.text: The Irish demonstrate the meaning of them

indicators.note: the opening words show, or demonstrate, the letters sitting within them

explanation.surface: Irish people illustrate what a word for 'them' means.
explanation.walkthrough: 'demonstrate' says the letters lie inside THE IRish; 'the meaning' only links to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: The possessive pronoun for a group means belonging to them.

clue.text: Blithe spirits of Shelley's dittos

parts.note: Shelley's poem To a Skylark opens 'Hail to thee, blithe spirit!', so many of those blithe spirits make a flock of larks, named by its collective noun

explanation.surface: A literary note on the cheerful beings in Shelley's verse.
explanation.walkthrough: Shelley's 'To a Skylark' calls the bird 'blithe spirit'; 'dittos' makes it plural, a flock of skylarks, whose collective noun is the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: The traditional collective noun for a gathering of larks is this word, meaning rapture.

clue.text: This mouse is a fly-by-night

parts.note: a bat is a mouse that flies at night, and its old name is formed by putting a word for one who flits before mouse

explanation.surface: A remark that some mouse is an untrustworthy, here-today-gone-tomorrow sort.
explanation.walkthrough: FLITTERMOUSE is an old name for the bat, the mouse that flies by night; one who flits, or does a moonlight flit, is a fly-by-night too.
explanation.definitionFit: One who flits about or decamps by night is a fly-by-night, and a bat is a flittermouse.

clue.text: First of nuclear missiles seen in the Straits ?

indicators.note: only the opening letter of the next word is wanted

parts.note: arrows are missiles shot from a bow

explanation.surface: Nuclear missiles spotted in some sea passage, a Cold War alarm.
explanation.walkthrough: 'seen in the' only links the wordplay to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A narrow stretch of water joining two seas is a strait, also called the narrows.

clue.text: It's the better way, of course

definitions.text: It's the better way, of course

parts.words: It's the better way, of course
parts.note: on a racecourse a punter can bet a horse to win and to be placed, a so-called way of betting that names a kind of wager

explanation.surface: Someone insisting that their method is naturally the superior one.
explanation.walkthrough: 'better' is one who bets and 'course' is a racecourse: an each-way bet backs a horse to win or be placed.
explanation.definitionFit: An each-way bet is a familiar way for a punter at the races to stake money.

clue.text: Demo not on time? Someone is late

definitions.text: Demo not on time? Someone is late

parts.words: Demo not on time? Someone is late
parts.note: a demonstration is a march, and one that is not quick is slow; 'the late' are the dead, honoured by a measured funeral procession

explanation.surface: A protest march running behind schedule because a participant is late.
explanation.walkthrough: 'late' looks like tardy but means deceased: this is the solemn pace of a funeral procession.
explanation.definitionFit: A solemn military pace used at funerals is the measured step of a procession honouring the dead.

clue.text: Robin resorting to fresher woods here

definitions.text: Robin resorting to fresher woods here

indicators.note: read as re-sorting, the letters are sorted again into a new order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: The outlaw hero heads off to greener woodland.
explanation.walkthrough: 'resorting' means going, but read re-sorting it rearranges TO FRESHER WOODS; the whole clue also describes Robin Hood's haunt.
explanation.definitionFit: The Nottinghamshire woodland is the legendary home of Robin Hood and his outlaws.

clue.text: Fish for the guard

definitions.meaning: a deep-sea rat-tail fish goes by this name
a soldier of a famous British Guards regiment

explanation.surface: A fish given as fit for a guardsman.
explanation.definitionFit: The deep-sea rat-tail fish shares its name with soldiers of the British Army's senior foot guards regiment.

clue.text: A well-filled church for the clergy

indicators.note: one piece has its middle filled by the other

parts.note: well can mean a lot, as in well over the limit

explanation.surface: A church full of worshippers, fitting for the priesthood.
explanation.walkthrough: 'filled' puts LOT inside CH; 'A' and 'for' only link.
explanation.definitionFit: Priests collectively are known by the term for their garb, as in 'a man of the cloth'.

clue.text: Ruth's wandering in part of 8

indicators.note: the letters stray from their order

parts.note: the name with its S counted as a letter

explanation.surface: Ruth goes wandering in Sherwood.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wandering' shuffles RUTHS. 8 is SHERWOOD FOREST.
explanation.definitionFit: A hurst is an old word for a wooded hill or copse, which is a piece of a forest.

clue.text: Weight test in ring? Just the opposite

indicators.note: one piece is set inside another
says to reverse what the clue states, so the ring goes inside the test rather than the test inside the ring

parts.note: to try is to test
O is a ring by its shape

explanation.surface: A weight test in a boxing ring, or rather the reverse.
explanation.walkthrough: Read literally, 'test in ring' would put TRY inside O; 'Just the opposite' turns that round, O inside TRY.
explanation.definitionFit: Troy weight is the traditional system used for precious metals and gems.

clue.text: Tent-maker found paradise in the wilderness

definitions.text: Tent-maker found paradise in the wilderness

parts.words: Tent-maker found paradise in the wilderness
parts.note: the Persian poet's surname means tent-maker, and in FitzGerald's Rubaiyat he says that with bread, wine and his love the wilderness were paradise enow

explanation.surface: A camping-gear craftsman discovers bliss out in the wild.
explanation.walkthrough: Khayyam means tent-maker; the Rubaiyat of Omar Khayyam has 'Oh, Wilderness were Paradise enow!'
explanation.definitionFit: The medieval Persian poet bore the name Khayyam, meaning tent-maker, and his quatrains praise wine in the wild.

clue.text: Where a sailor' can get a home for a song?

definitions.text: Where a sailor' can get a home for a song

parts.words: Where a sailor' can get a home for a song
parts.note: a sailor's song is a sea shanty, and a home got for a song is a very cheap one in a slum of makeshift huts

explanation.surface: A tip about cheap housing for seamen.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for a song' means cheaply, but also suggests the sailor's working song, the shanty.
explanation.definitionFit: A settlement of crude makeshift shacks, usually on a city's edge, is called by this name.

clue.text: Mercy at the day of reckoning

definitions.meaning: clemency shown to a beaten enemy, as in to give no such thing
a ... day, one of the four days each year when rents and accounts fall due

explanation.surface: A plea for mercy when judgment day arrives.
explanation.walkthrough: In Britain the quarter days were the dates rent and debts were settled, hence days of reckoning.
explanation.definitionFit: Clemency to a defeated foe is given or refused, and a quarter day is when rents and accounts were settled.

clue.text: A leaf, if it is developed into a branch

indicators.note: the letters are worked up into a new form

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A leaf, given time, grows into a twig.
explanation.walkthrough: 'developed' rearranges A LEAF, IF and IT; 'is' and 'into' only link.
explanation.definitionFit: A subsidiary office or associated company is an affiliate, linked to the parent organisation.

clue.text: Lively school-half with zero vandalism

indicators.note: only the first half of the word is kept
wrecking the word smashes its letters into a new order

explanation.surface: A rowdy half of a school with no respect for property.
explanation.walkthrough: 'half' takes SCH from school; 'vandalism' wrecks ZERO into ERZO.
explanation.definitionFit: A scherzo is a quick, playful movement in a symphony or sonata.

clue.text: Tangled hair of a periwig?

parts.note: a peri is a fairy, as an elf is, and a wig is made of locks of hair

explanation.surface: A wig that has got into a tangle.
explanation.walkthrough: Split as PERI WIG, a periwig is a fairy's hairpiece, so a fairy's tangled lock of hair.
explanation.definitionFit: A matted knot of hair was once blamed on elves tangling it at night.

clue.text: Indispensable fish, we hear, upsetting the boat

indicators.note: the words are judged by how they are spoken

parts.note: indispensable means key, and ling is a fish of the cod family

explanation.surface: A crucial fish, apparently, capsizing the vessel.
explanation.walkthrough: KEY LING said aloud gives the word for keeling over.
explanation.definitionFit: A boat that keels over is turning on its side and capsizing.

clue.text: Hard-pressed to get the piano gradually shifted?

parts.note: P is the musical abbreviation for piano, softly
inched means moved little by little

explanation.surface: Struggling to edge a piano along little by little.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to get the' only links the definition and wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Being short of money or strained is to be pinched, squeezed hard.

clue.text: Build-up of security for airborne mascot?

parts.note: a para is a paratrooper, an airborne soldier
a regiment's mascot is its pet

explanation.surface: Raising security for a parachuting regimental mascot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for' only links the definition and wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: A low protective wall raised along a roof or rampart is built up for safety.

clue.text: Ring for a 7, perhaps

parts.note: 7 is a slow march, the pace of a funeral, for which a bell is rung slowly

explanation.surface: An instruction to ring a bell for some numbered occasion.
explanation.walkthrough: 7 is SLOW MARCH, the pace of a funeral; a bell is rung slowly and steadily for it.
explanation.definitionFit: A bell rung slowly for a death or funeral is said to sound this way.

clue.text: This animal put back to grass

indicators.note: the letters are set back to front

parts.note: a reed is a tall grass

explanation.surface: A creature returned to pasture.
explanation.walkthrough: 'put back' turns REED round.
explanation.definitionFit: A deer is a grazing hoofed animal such as a stag.

clue.text: Swift race. It's a brute !

definitions.meaning: the brutish humanlike creatures in Jonathan Swift's Gulliver's Travels

explanation.surface: A fast race, won by a beast.
explanation.walkthrough: Swift is the author Jonathan Swift, not speed.
explanation.definitionFit: Swift's Gulliver meets these brutish creatures, and the name became a word for a boorish lout.

clue.text: He embraces a German poet

indicators.note: one piece hugs the other inside it

parts.note: taken as written
ein is German for a

explanation.surface: A man hugs a German poet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'embraces' puts EIN inside HE.
explanation.definitionFit: Heinrich Heine was the nineteenth-century German lyric writer of the Buch der Lieder.

clue.text: He heard order to prepare for prayer

indicators.note: the words are judged by how they are spoken

parts.note: the command to get down on one's knees, as before praying

explanation.surface: A man hears a call to get ready to pray.
explanation.walkthrough: KNEEL said aloud gives the man's name.
explanation.definitionFit: He stands for a man, and Neil is a man's first name.

clue.text: Stand up and applaud one at the Eisteddfod

definitions.meaning: a member of one of the orders of the Welsh Gorsedd of bards

explanation.surface: A standing ovation for a performer at a Welsh festival.
explanation.walkthrough: The Eisteddfod is the Welsh festival of poetry and music, whose Gorsedd has bards, druids and ovates.
explanation.definitionFit: To give an ovation is to ovate, and an ovate is a member of a rank of the Welsh bardic order.

clue.text: To do better' without is to make do with what one has

definitions.text: make do with what one has

indicators.note: old sense of outside: the first piece goes outside the second

parts.note: to improve is to do better
taken as written

explanation.surface: Doing better without something means managing with what you have.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' is the old sense outside: IMPROVE goes round IS.
explanation.definitionFit: To manage with whatever materials are at hand, inventing as you go.

clue.text: Revelation maybe thin gentlemen provide, how to lose weight ?

indicators.note: suggests the words could be arranged otherwise

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Slim men explaining how they shed the pounds.
explanation.walkthrough: 'maybe' rearranges THIN GENTLEMEN; the tail adds that lightening men is how to lose weight.
explanation.definitionFit: Enlightenment is a sudden insight or spiritual awakening, a disclosure of truth.
